newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Philippine peso closes weaker on arbitrage play.
newsitem.headline: Philippine peso closes weaker on arbitrage play.

text.p: The Philippine peso closed lower at 26.384 to the dollar against Thursday's 26.373 on the usual weekend arbitrage play, traders said.
Turnover was heavy at $348.50 million as banks sold their dollars for settlement-Friday, and bought them back in the afternoon for settlement Monday.
Banks which bought dollars value-Monday will be able to earn the relatively high interest rates on their peso holdings over the weekend before paying them out on Monday.
Value-Friday deals were wedged between 26.368 and 26.369. The Central Bank was seen buying dollars at 26.369.
For value-Monday deals, banks were trading between 26.385 and 26.383 throughout the day. Some banks were on the sell side due to the steady inflow of foreign exchange, one trader said.
The Central Bank had to intervene by buying dollars at 26.384 to prevent the peso from appreciating too fast.
Traders estimated the Central Bank had bought $95 million in late afternoon.
They expected the peso-dollar exchange rate to return to the 26.375 on Monday.
